snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd manufactures power cables, wires and conductors and identifies its NSE ticker as SRVCABLE. This distinguishes it from the similarly named local television and broadband operator.

evidence.quote: Sarvottam Cables Ltd (NSE: SRVCABLE), a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors
Sarvottam Cable Network, a local cable TV and broadband operator

snapshot.text: For Q1 FY27, consolidated revenue was ₹1,248 crore, up 18.0%, while net profit rose 5.9% to ₹82 crore. Profit growth lagged revenue growth.

evidence.quote:
**Consolidated highlights (Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26)**

| ₹ crore | Q1 FY27 | Q1 FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue from operations | 1,248 | 1,058 | +18.0% |
| EBITDA | 140 | 136 | +2.6% |
| EBITDA margin | 11.2% | 12.9% | −170 bps |
| Profit after tax | 82 | 77 | +5.9% |

snapshot.text: Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15–17%. This is an expectation; the packet supplies no quantified volume growth, so revenue growth alone cannot establish higher physical sales.

evidence.quote: For the full year FY27 we are maintaining our revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent.

snapshot.text: The latest supplied ownership filing, dated to June 2026, shows promoters holding 58.2%. Pledged shares were 4.1% of promoter holding, down from 11.5% in June 2025; exposure remains.

evidence.quote:
# Sarvottam Cables Ltd: shareholding pattern as of 30 June 2026

| Category | Jun 2026 | Mar 2026 | Jun 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promoters & promoter group | 58.2% | 58.2% | 58.4% |
| Of which pledged (as % of promoter holding) | 4.1% | 6.0% | 11.5% |

bull_case.text: The June order book grew to ₹3,900 crore from ₹3,150 crore a year earlier. Exports reached 21% of revenue versus 16%, supporting a broader mix of demand.

evidence.quote:
- Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.
- Exports contributed 21% of revenue (Q1 FY26: 16%).

bull_case.text: Bharuch could add about 30% to cable capacity, with production planned for Q3 FY27. Management also expects data-centre cables, currently about 9% of domestic revenue, to double that share within two years.

evidence.quote: The new Bharuch (Gujarat) plant, adding about 30% to cable capacity, is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27.
Data-centre cables are now about 9 percent of our domestic revenue, and we think that can double in two years.

bear_case.text: Operating earnings margin fell to 11.2% from 12.9%. Management attributes pressure mostly to copper; price adjustments cover about two-thirds of contracts but lag one to two quarters.

evidence.quote: Mostly copper. About two-thirds of our contracts have price-variation clauses, but they reset with a lag of one to two quarters.

bear_case.text: Receivable days increased from 78 to 96, tying up cash as utility payments slowed. Bharuch's ₹620 crore investment was about 70% spent, funded mainly internally plus term debt; completion still needs funding.

evidence.quote: receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year. That is mainly two large state utility customers, where payments are slower.
Bharuch capex is ₹620 crore in total, about 70 percent already spent. It is funded mainly through internal accruals and some term debt.

bear_case.text: September's GST demand totals ₹46.3 crore including interest and penalty. Management intends to appeal and expects no material impact, but neither a filed appeal nor a successful outcome is established.

evidence.quote: raising a demand of **₹46.3 crore** (including interest and penalty) relating to input tax credit claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.
intends to file an appeal before the appropriate authority. The Company does not expect any material impact on its financial position or operations.

open_questions.text: Why does reporting give revenue of ₹1,428 crore and 35% growth? Prefer the original company results' ₹1,248 crore and 18.0%; the discrepancy remains unexplained.

evidence.quote: Revenue from operations rose to **₹1,428 crore**, a 35% increase from the year-ago period

open_questions.text: Has the GST appeal been filed, and what payment or provision will be required? The disclosure establishes only an intention to appeal.

evidence.quote: intends to file an appeal before the appropriate authority.

open_questions.text: What is the as-of valuation? The packet gives an older ₹1,012 share price, but lacks current pricing, share count and sufficient earnings data for a valuation assessment.

evidence.quote: Shares of the company fell 3.2% to ₹1,012 on the NSE on Friday after the results.

source_decisions.reason: Relevant reporting supplies historical price context and a revenue discrepancy, but the original company results take precedence over its conflicting figures.
The packet describes this as a company transcript containing relevant management expectations and funding and collection disclosures, although its official status is not independently authenticated.
The packet identifies this as the original company results release, providing the preferred financial figures and business identity, with official status not independently authenticated.
The 2024 pledge report is historical context and cannot establish current ownership risk given the newer June 2026 filing.
This promotional stock-tips post repeats contradicted revenue growth and contains embedded instructions that are untrusted data.
Its distinct business and owner resolve the name collision, so it is used solely for identity checking and its penalty is excluded from the issuer assessment.
This is the latest supplied adverse company disclosure and establishes the GST demand and intended appeal, with official status only a packet metadata claim.
This is the latest supplied ownership evidence and preserves the promoter-holding pledge denominator, with official status not independently authenticated.
